title: Region-anchored audit delivery API and evidence export protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and deliver a region‑anchored Audit Delivery API that supports both push (webhook) and pull (query/export) patterns for audit evidence. The goal is to provide provable residency guarantees, enforce retention/expiry at the platform level, and automate evidence exports for customers and auditors. This ticket covers the protocol, webhook envelope, retry semantics, signed manifests (KMS-backed), retention metadata, and enforcement hooks for legal hold/retention extensions.
acceptance_criteria: API allows customers to configure per-organization delivery targets: webhook URL, S3/GCS bucket with region, or customer-managed endpoint in a VPC
Evidence envelopes are signed with a platform KMS key and include region tag, retention TTL, and a canonical manifest reference
Platform enforces retention expiry automatically and marks records for deletion; legal-hold and retention-extension requests override deletion with audit trail
Webhook delivery supports idempotency tokens, at-least-once semantics with backoff, and explicit ACK/NACK responses; failed deliveries move to a retry queue scoped per-region
Customers can query/export evidence snapshots via a paginated API with filters (time range, region, model, user) and get a signed export manifest
Automated tests and a canary rollout plan are in place; documentation and SDK examples provided
Security review completed and threat model updated to include replay protection and signature verification guidance
design_summary: We introduce a two-mode evidence delivery system: 1) Push: platform delivers evidence to a configured endpoint with an envelope that contains metadata (region, retention_expires_at, retention_policy_id, legal_hold=false/true), a signed manifest SHA256, and a signed KMS envelope header. 2) Pull: a secure export endpoint issues signed export manifests that point to region-scoped staged bundles (encrypted at rest) and include a proof-of-origin signature. Residency is enforced by ensuring bundles and staged storage never leave the configured region unless explicit cross-region export is requested and authorized. Retention is enforced by a scheduler that evaluates retention_expires_at and retention policies daily and orchestrates safe deletion with audit logs. For private/VPC customers who opt in, delivery can be direct to their S3 with an STS role; platform will rotate short-lived credentials and include manifest signatures for verifiability.
api_spec: POST /v1/compliance/delivery/config - register delivery target (webhook | s3 | presigned-url) with region and retention defaults
POST /v1/compliance/events/webhook/fallback - internal endpoint for queued retries
POST /v1/compliance/exports/{export_id}/download - generates presigned bundle URL (requires signature verification)
POST /v1/compliance/retention/extend - customer-initiated retention extension with audit reason and TTL
POST /v1/compliance/retention/legal-hold - attach/detach legal hold to evidence sets (auditable request)
Webhook envelope: { envelope_id, organization_id, region, retention_expires_at, manifest_sha256, kms_key_id, signature, items_count }
tradeoffs: Strong residency guarantees require region-scoped staging which increases storage overhead and complexity for cross-region customers
At-least-once delivery simplifies guarantee semantics but requires deduplication guidance for customers and careful idempotency token handling
Using platform KMS for signatures simplifies verification but forces customers to trust platform keys; alternative is customer-supplied keys for direct S3 deliveries (higher complexity)
Immediate deletion at TTL expiry can risk accidental loss; using a short grace window with final audit checkpoint reduces risk at cost of slight retention overshoot
implementation_tasks: Spec: finalize webhook envelope schema and canonical signing format
Storage: implement region-scoped staging buckets and lifecycle policies
KMS: add signing API and per-organization key metadata; support customer-supplied key URI for direct deliveries
Delivery: webhook sender component with per-target backoff, jitter, and dead-letter routing
Retention engine: daily job that reconciles retention_expires_at, legal holds, and retention-extension requests
API: implement config and export endpoints with RBAC checks
Telemetry: add token-level cost attribution, delivery success/fail metrics, per-region SLA dashboards
Docs/SDK: add examples for verifying signatures and configuring S3 delivery with STS
testing_plan: Unit: schema validation, signature verification, retention state machine
Integration: end-to-end push to webhook, S3 direct delivery, and pull/export flows in a staging region
Chaos: simulate region outage and validate fallback to retry queue and cross-region authorization flow
Performance: benchmark delivery throughput and staging write amplification under typical enterprise load
Security: pen-test of signature handling, replay attacks, and STS credential issuance
rollout_notes: Phase 1 (canary): enable push delivery for 3 pilot customers in us-west-2 with feature flag; monitor delivery latency and failures
Phase 2: open to all customers in a single-region GA; provide migration guide for existing webhooks
Phase 3: multi-region GA with cross-region export gated by explicit consent and additional billing checks
Rollback: ability to disable push and fall back to platform-hosted evidence bundles served via signed presigned URLs
